hints: Think backwards from the ester, an ester splits into its acid part and its alcohol part at the C-O single bond.
Look at the two identical end groups, the O is joined to a carbon bonded to two methyl groups, so work out if that alcohol carbon is primary, secondary or tertiary.
Focus on the central six-membered ring, check if it has double bonds like benzene or only single bonds like cyclohexane to decide if it is planar or puckered.
walkthrough:
**Split Ester Z Back Into Acid + Alcohol**

Think of esterification in reverse. Each ester link breaks to give back a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.

$$\text{R-COOH} + \text{R'-OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{R-COOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify And Classify Alcohol X**

The O-alkyl part on both ends is $-\text{O-CH(CH}_3)_2$. That comes from propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$.

The C bonded to OH is bonded to two other carbons, so it is a secondary alcohol.

**Identify Acid Y And The Shape Of Its Ring**

The acid part is the central ring with two $-\text{COOH}$ groups, which is cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

The ring has only C-C single bonds, so every ring carbon is $sp^3$. Cyclohexane adopts a puckered chair shape and is non-planar, unlike flat benzene with delocalised $sp^2$ carbons.

options.A: Correct. X is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol, and Y contains a saturated cyclohexane ring which is non-planar due to tetrahedral sp3 carbons.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. The alcohol is correctly secondary, but the ring is not planar. Students choose this if they mistake the saturated cyclohexane ring for a benzene ring.
options.C: Half right but half wrong. The ring is correctly non-planar, but the alcohol is not tertiary. The O is attached to CH with two methyls, not C with three methyls, so it is secondary, not 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
options.D: Both parts wrong. The end group is not $(CH3)3C-O-$, so X is not tertiary, and the central ring has no C=C double bonds, so it is not flat and aromatic like benzene.
